title: Soar into a successful aviation career with Black Hawk College and Quad Cities Aero - NewsBreak
text:
By Riley Hemmer ,
5 hours ago
There is still a pilot shortage being seen across the United States, but here in the QCA, a new college program hopes to fix that issue.
Black Hawk College is collaborating with Quad Cities Aero , owned by Summer Kuehl, to launch the Professional Aero Certification (PAC) Program .
Kuehl answers what the program is:
Kuehl details how long the program is, and who it’s aimed to benefit:
The program will train students to become flight instructors after 16 months.
“It’s a way for them to get it done in an accelerated format without compromising any of the integrity of training,” says Kuehl.
Kuehl found a passion for aviation thanks to a client of hers here in the Quad Cities.
“I joke that it’s my quarter-life crisis, I did not grow up in aviation at all,” says Kuehl. “I was selling insurance in the area. One day, it was like a Friday afternoon, and [my client] took me up. I was like, ‘this is insane’, I did not know that this world existed.”
After switching careers, Kuehl opened QC Aero with her husband Kyle.
“He’s a business owner, so he convinced me,” says Kuehl. “He said, ‘you know there’s a need in the Quad Cities for flight instruction, so why don’t you just start your own flight instruction business?'”
They’ve been busy since opening in 2020.
“Now I’ve got three airplanes, 3 Cessna 172’s, and we’ve got eight instructors,” says Kuehl.
While QC Aero has grown, the aviation industry is shrinking.
“We’ve never seen a market this vast. The workforce demand for the next 15 years is expected to be at crisis levels, and it’s because baby boomers are retiring,” says Chris Johnson, PAC Program Manager.
Out of his seven previous program openings, Johnson is looking forward to this one – it’s close to home.
“I’m actually from the Quad Cities area, I actually grew up in Clinton, Iowa.”
Aviation research firms estimate a shortage of 29,000 pilots by 2032.
“We’re in dire need of good talent in aviation. It’s a growing space, and we really need people who are excited about aviation to get involved in it,” says Kuehl.
The program is hosting an open house on Oct. 15 at the Quad Cities International Airport.
